Only −8/27 is not positive; check: sqrt(64/9) = 8/3 = −9(−8/27). Choice A is the extraneous solution created by squaring.

The graph of y = f(x) + 2 has a y-intercept of 4 and levels off near y = 5 on the left, which matches y = −5^x + 5 (at x = 0, −1 + 5 = 4). Since f(x) + 2 = −5^x + 5, we get f(x) = −5^x + 3. Choice D is the equation of the graph itself, not of f.

A side 70% shorter is 30% of the original: 0.30 × 45 = 13.5 inches. The same 45 × 13 = 585 miles now fits in 13.5 inches, so 1 inch represents 585/13.5 ≈ 43.33 miles. Choice A (3.90) multiplies 13 by 0.30, but a smaller map must cover more miles per inch, not fewer.

Set each factor to 0: x = 0 (from 7x^2), x = 13/4, and x = u/4. Their sum is 0 + 13/4 + u/4 = (13 + u)/4 = 25, so 13 + u = 100 and u = 87. The zero solution adds nothing to the sum even though it is repeated.

For similar solids, the ratio of surface areas is the square of the scale factor: 1,475/59 = 25, so Y is 5 times as large as X in each dimension. Volumes scale by 5^3 = 125, so the volume of X is 1,500/125 = 12. The sum is 1,500 + 12 = 1,512.
